memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "At this, they tore their clothes. Then they all loaded their donkeys and went back to the city." — Gen 44:13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This single verse may be one of the most important in the whole Joseph story. Tearing your clothes was the deepest expression of grief a person could make. And the brothers all do it — every one of them.

Understand what has just happened. Legally, they are free to go. The steward said so: whoever is found with the cup becomes a slave, the rest are free from blame. They could load their donkeys and ride home. Benjamin's fate would be his own. Nobody in Egypt would stop them.

Twenty years earlier, that is precisely what they did. They watched a brother taken away and then sat down to eat a meal.

But not this time. Not one of them leaves. They tear their clothes and they all turn back towards the city — walking straight into trouble they could have avoided, because they will not abandon their brother.

This is what repentance actually looks like. It is not a feeling or an apology. It is being placed in the same situation as before and choosing differently. God has been quietly working in these men for two decades, and here, on a dusty road outside an Egyptian city, the fruit finally appears.

God is patient. He is still working in you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What does this verse show you about the difference between regret and real repentance?
2. Where has God given you a second chance to respond differently than you once did?
3. Is there someone you have been tempted to walk away from when you should turn back?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for Your patience with me over years and years. Do the deep work in me that turns sorrow into real change, and give me the courage to turn back instead of walking away. Amen.
